Signed, Richard Mason.’’ ‘That—if a genuine document—may prove I have been married, but it does not prove that the woman mentioned therein as my wife is still living.’ ‘She was living three months ago,’ returned the lawyer. ‘How do you know?’ ‘I have a witness to the fact, whose testimony even you, sir, will scarcely controvert.’ ‘Produce him—or go to hell.’ ‘I will produce him first—he is on the spot. Mr. Mason, have the goodness to step forward.’ Mr. Rochester, on hearing the name, set his teeth; he experienced, too, a sort of strong convulsive quiver; near to him as I was, I felt the spasmodic movement of fury or despair run through his frame. The second stranger, who had hitherto lingered in the background, now drew near; a pale face looked over the solicitor’s shoulder—yes, it was Mason himself. Mr. Rochester turned and glared at him.
